title: unknown vs any vs never in TypeScript

scenes.say: You’ve seen unknown, any, and never. But when should you use each one?

scenes.label: any
scenes.sub: Disables all type checks. Use with caution.
scenes.say: Any turns off TypeScript’s type checking. It’s risky and can lead to runtime bugs.
Unknown is safer. You have to check the type before using it. Any lets you do anything, but that’s dangerous.

scenes.label: never
scenes.sub: Means a value never occurs. Used for unreachable code.
scenes.say: Never is for things that never happen, like a function that always throws or unreachable code.

scenes.question: What’s safer for API data?
scenes.right: Use unknown and validate before using. That keeps your code safe.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for the trap. Unknown is safer for external data. Always validate before you use it.
